topics.label: Introduction and lecture learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This topic provides the opening framing and learning objectives for the lecture on cancer causation.

topics.label: Genetic, environmental, and stochastic contributions to cancer development
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the conceptual foundations of cancer etiology by examining how genetic predisposition, endogenous replication errors, environmental exposures, and epidemiological patterns shape cancer incidence.

topics.label: Infectious agents and viral oncogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how biological pathogens drive malignant transformation, focusing on the cooperative viral and environmental etiology of Burkitt lymphoma.

topics.label: Chemical and physical mutagens and mechanisms of DNA damage
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how physical radiation and chemical compounds undergo metabolic activation to generate DNA adducts, mutations, and oxidative stress.

topics.label: Tumour promotion, host susceptibility, and mechanisms of carcinogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how non-mutagenic tumor promoters, chronic inflammation, and host developmental susceptibility cooperate to drive malignant outgrowth.

topics.label: Methodologies for identifying carcinogens and evaluating cancer risk
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the genomic, epidemiological, and experimental methods used to determine carcinogenicity and assess human exposure risks.

topics.label: Lecture summary and conclusion
topics.groupedBecause: This topic provides the closing summary and final conclusions for the lecture.
